shape: design/specs/domain/interfaces.md § What the apps ask of the engine
notes: the reading party: who I am, my display unit, what I have disclosed (stories 10, 11, 42)
`first-run` is `party: null` — no identity yet, which is what story 10 is about
`naming` is an identity that exists but has no name yet — what ChooseName is about. Without it that screen is unreachable by link: `first-run` has no identity, so the gate lands on Welcome instead.

NOT called `empty`: a variant name is global, and `empty` has to mean 'this screen has no data'. A party with no identity gates the whole app into onboarding, so `?variant=empty` on any screen would have shown first run instead of that screen's empty state.
mock writes (creating an identity, setting a name) are held in memory and do not survive a restart

`devices` is what can act as this party (story 13). `kind` is what it is to a person, not what it is to a machine; `contributes` is story 14's split — durability is a copy of the party's own records, availability is something that stays on. A phone contributes the first and not the second
`thisDevice` marks the one in the party's hand, so a list of three is not three identifiers to decode

`reachable: false` on the tablet is story 13's error variant: a device that cannot be reached at the moment it needs retiring. It is reached by acting rather than by a different world, so it needs no fixture of its own

`party.single-device.json` serves both `empty` and `error`: a party whose only machine is the phone in their hand. Story 13 path A, story 14 path A, and story 43 path B are the same party seen from three screens
`hostedBy: null` is a machine the party runs themselves. Story 14 path B keeps hosting by somebody else a separate decision, so it is a separate field rather than a kind
